answer.sameness: Every page is the same split hero: top-left wordmark + 'Domov' link, big left-aligned headline (3–4 lines), one short paragraph, a small pill button, and a single decorative element on the right (thin line-art icon or an AI photo with an 'Ustvarjeno z UI' badge). Type is two families only: a geometric grotesk (Bergant, Ovinek, Jasna, Kodra, Rov, Takt, Vrhovnik) and a serif (Simnu, Tič, Pinterič), all at near-identical sizes. Palettes alternate white/off-white vs. near-black with one accent; the pink/magenta button recurs (Bergant, Kodra, Takt). Line icons share one stroke weight and style. Mobile pages all end in the same Klic / Navodila za pot button bar.
recurringIssues: Right half of the hero is empty or filled with a single thin line drawing, so desktop first screens feel underpopulated (Ovinek, Jasna, Tič, Pinterič, Simnu).
Headline and body sizes are nearly identical across pages, giving one voice regardless of trade.
AI-generated stock photos with a visible 'Ustvarjeno z UI' badge undermine trust (Bergant, Kodra, Vrhovnik).
Tiny pill buttons and link-sized CTAs have weak prominence against large headlines.
Mobile screens cut off awkwardly: Pinterič shows a clipped section title, Takt phone/button overlap, Jasna has a dead blue band.
Sticky bottom bar on mobile hides content and is identical on every site.
Light grey small body text has marginal contrast on dark pages.

best.why: Dark green, warm yellow serif and the bold cheese-wheel graphic feel genuinely tied to the business and carry the strongest colour identity.
The serif type and oversized clock face give a quiet, craft-like mood that matches a watchmaker and holds up on mobile.
The hanging-lamp line drawing and amber accent create a believable atmosphere for an ex-mine brewery.

weakest.why: The green bent pipe shape means nothing, the address block clutters the top, and the right side is mostly empty.
Headline floats in a vast empty beige field with a sketch tucked in the corner; mobile shows a clipped heading.
Blue service strip and tiny glasses icon sit awkwardly, leaving large dead areas and a stray empty blue band on mobile.

answer.oneChange: Break the single hero template: give each business its own composition, type scale and image treatment (real photography, bespoke illustration or full-bleed colour), instead of swapping accent colour and a line icon in the same left-text/right-ornament layout.
answer.summary: This batch is clean, legible and consistently built, but it is one template wearing ten outfits. Every homepage uses the same left-aligned headline, short paragraph, small button and a lone right-side ornament; only the colour and a line icon change. Three pages use obviously AI-generated photos with a visible label. The dark, serif-led pages (cheese dairy, watchmaker, brewery) show the studio can create mood; the light pages (bike shop, optician, winery) feel empty and generic. To move from a template shop to a studio owners would be proud of, invest in distinct hero compositions, varied type scales, and real or bespoke imagery, and fix the mobile cut-offs and overlapping buttons.
